doc.title: Mose Allison — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Sitting in everywhere, and Denver with Cedar Walton and Shelly Rym
summary: Audre marvels at his habit of asking to sit in; in Denver he traded pianos with Cedar Walton and wrote for Shelly Rym.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: I remember that when you came to St. Louis, anywhere we ever went, I was always like shocked that you would just go up and say, “Can I sit in?”—and they would always let you. Then they would always love it. I’d never seen that happen before with anybody. And as shy as Mose is, he’s pretty...
Yeah. The fact that he would always do that surprised me.
And in Denver... And you often got work that way, too. Cedar Walton, wasn’t he...
Oh, you met Cedar Walton in Denver?
Yeah. I used to play in a band with him.
You played trumpet in that band?

Well, Cedar and I used to trade pianos. Shelly Rym was the name of the guy that we worked for. Shelly Rym. I remember him. [LAUGHS] I wrote arrangements for him for a small band that his wife sang in.
So you were all-purpose. You played trumpet, you played piano, you wrote arrangements for various size ensembles.
